title: Consider making (un)registerProtocolHandler asynchronous
body:
@mikewest @annevk 

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/system-state.html#custom-handlers

Currently, (un)registerProtocolHandler may throw SyntaxError or SecurityError exceptions after parsing the arguments.

However, registration may also fail for any other reason e.g. if the users reject the request or has a preference to do that. Handling this cannot be done synchronously, and moreover typically happens in a separate process dedicated to UI. 

Currently, it is not possible for the JS code to easily determine if/when such registration failure happens. This is not nice for web developer or for writing automated tests. One can still do that by regularly checking if a clicking a link with a custom protocol redirects to the registered url (in particular exposing it does not seem to add fingerprinting issue) but that's not very convenient.

It seems to me the signature of (un)registerProtocolHandler could be easily changed to return a promise instead of undefined. As long as we keep the SyntaxError and SecurityError exceptions synchronous, that shouldn't break backward compatibility.

The alternative to add a callback argument is not very aligned with "modern" approach, and even worse since the status of https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/5425 is not really clear on Mozilla's side atm

Any thought?
